argument.notes: At every finite positive scale the admissible countable covers coincide, with identical extended nonnegative costs and sums, hence identical infima. The ∞-scale admissible class contains the scale-1 class, so its infimum is bounded by an already included content; taking suprema proves F001 without a normalization change or limit exchange. S002 correctly derives each clause of F002. Nonnegativity in S003 follows from the dimension's codomain, also for A=∅ and m=0.

statement_closure.notes: D001–D004 specify the diameter, countable-cover contents, native measure and extended nonnegative dimension needed by all statements. N001 quantifies m, A⊆R^m and s>0 and exports the exact equality and four conditional consequences proved here. The costs at empty sets, positive-exponent zero diameters, finite versus infinite scales, and nonnegative dimension codomain are explicit. background_notes.fact: For an at most countable indexed family of sets with nonnegative extended real costs, one can preserve every index once in an enumeration by natural numbers, padding unused positions by empty sets of cost zero. The union and total cost are unchanged. Conversely every sequence is a countable cover. This remains valid for an empty or finite family and for an infinite total cost.

grounds.reason: D002 uses countable covers with nonnegative costs and zero cost for empty members.
M001 uses sequences indexed by natural numbers, with the same zero cost for empty members.
S001 compares precisely these two cover presentations at a fixed finite positive scale.

background_notes.justification: Inject the countable index set into ℕ, place each original member at its assigned position, and put ∅ elsewhere. Union membership is unchanged. A sum of nonnegative terms is the supremum of its finite subsums, which are unchanged by this injection and zero padding. Thus the comparison preserves costs even when the sum is infinite; no enumeration of the covered set A is involved.

background_notes.fact: For a finite scale δ>0 and s>0 in Euclidean space, every set U with extended diameter at most δ has a finite diameter d∈[0,δ]. On nonempty U its extended nonnegative real power d^s is the image of the ordinary real power, including 0^s=0; empty members have zero cost by the stated conventions.

grounds.reason: The ambient space is Euclidean R^m for an arbitrary natural m.
The exponent s is a positive real.
D001 identifies finite extended Euclidean diameter with its ordinary nonnegative real value.
D002 restricts each cover member's diameter to the positive real scale δ and assigns zero empty-set cost.
M001 has the same diameter restriction and explicitly assigns empty-set cost zero.

background_notes.justification: A nonempty such U is bounded: fixing x∈U, every y∈U satisfies dist(x,y)≤diam(U)≤δ. Its distance supremum is therefore finite and agrees with D001's real diameter. On a positive finite d, both real-power conventions use exp(s log d), and at d=0 both give zero because s>0. Together with the separate empty-set rule, the two formulas have equal costs on every admissible member.
